user.title: Electricity Lens
user.description:
Computes the consumption, electricity mix, and costs of your household and of each device. If you like, also what your PV plant, heat pump, and electric car have saved, and when they pay for themselves.

From your energy dashboard:
{grid} Grid import with electricity price
{export} Feed-in
{compensation} Feed-in compensation
✓ Solar: {solar} sources
{battery} Battery
✓ Individual devices: {devices}

household.title: Household
household.description: All optional. The standing charge is added to the grid costs. With price levels you see how much grid power you drew in cheap and in expensive hours.

data_description.standing_charge: As on the electricity bill; shared evenly over the hours of the month
data_description.cheap_until: Grid power at this price or below counts as cheap, if a higher price occurred within the last 24 hours
data_description.expensive_from: Grid power at this price or above counts as expensive, if a lower price occurred within the last 24 hours

pv.title: PV plant
pv.description: Counted from {since}, when Home Assistant's solar data begins. Production, feed-in, battery, and electricity prices come from the energy dashboard.

pv_no_export.title: PV plant
pv_no_export.description:
**The energy dashboard has no feed-in.** All solar power then counts as used in the house.

Counted from {since}, when Home Assistant's solar data begins. Production, feed-in, battery, and electricity prices come from the energy dashboard.

wallbox.title: Electric car
wallbox.description: Compares the electric car with a combustion car, if you like. What is charged at the wallbox is measured.

data_description.comparison: Nothing, as for a second car: no saving, but charging costs and mix
data_description.investment: Extra purchase cost over a combustion car. For the payback.

wallbox_values.title: Average since {since}
wallbox_values.description: For the time since {since}, Home Assistant knows neither fuel prices nor consumptions. Enter averages. They also apply from now on, until you change them.

data_description.ev_consumption: At the wallbox with charging losses, usually 10–15 % above the car's display. With several cars, their average.
data_description.combustion_consumption: What a comparable combustion car would have used
data_description.tariff: Only with a separate tariff for the car; otherwise the energy dashboard's price counts
data_description.fuel_price_entity: Replaces the average from now on

wallbox_values_none.title: Average since {since}
wallbox_values_none.description: Without a comparison there is no saving. Electricity Lens shows the charging costs, their mix, and the average price. A tariff of your own applies since {since} and from now on, until you change it.

data_description.tariff: Only with a separate tariff for the car; otherwise the energy dashboard's price counts

error.scop_range: Enter a seasonal COP between 1 and 10.
error.investment_without_comparison: Without a comparison there is no saving to pay back an extra cost. Leave it empty.

abort.no_energy_dashboard: First set up the grid import with an electricity price in the [energy dashboard](/config/energy). Then you can add Electricity Lens.
abort.energy_interface: The energy dashboard cannot be read. This version of Home Assistant is not supported yet; please look for an update of Electricity Lens.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Electricity Lens is already set up. Add more on its integration page.

create_entry.default: The past is now being computed; with several years of data this can take a few minutes. Add the dashboard "Electricity Lens" under [Settings › Dashboards](/config/lovelace/dashboards) › "Add dashboard". Its cards are also under "Add card".

no_grid_price.title: Electricity Lens is missing the electricity price
